headline: NEW to scans -- Ukraine says Starlink/Starshield fully restored after 10+ days of throttling
dek: Ukraine said on Saturday Oct 24 that Starlink and its military version Starshield are again operating at pre-restriction speeds after more than a week (restrictions began Oct 14) of throttling that capped operations at 160 kph, hampered drone-interceptor operations and forced cancellations.…
sources: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Telegram) + Ukraine Defence Ministry (Telegram), via Reuters (Yuliia Dysa); Al Jazeera Oct 24 piece
fault_line: Who should control an army's internet — a private billionaire, or the state paying for the war? Social debate is dominated by distrust of Trump/Musk statements ('lying, again') and calls to replace Starlink.

sections.what_happened: Ukraine said on Saturday Oct 24 that Starlink and its military version Starshield are again operating at pre-restriction speeds after more than a week (restrictions began Oct 14) of throttling that capped operations at 160 kph, hampered drone-interceptor operations and forced cancellations. Zelenskyy: restoration began overnight Oct 23-24. Defence Ministry: monitoring systems record stable connectivity above 400 kph. The restrictions followed Trump's Russian-diesel deal announcement and pressure on Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries. Neither Musk nor the US government has acknowledged responsibility for the restriction; each has said only the other could have ordered it. The ministry did not say service was fully restored, only speeds. AJ adds: who ordered the restrictions remains unclear; Trump denied responsibility while defending Musk.
sections.what_verified: Reuters wire (carried by WNCY/WDSM/TBS/941/965 = 1 family) + Al Jazeera (own Oct 24 piece) + Jerusalem Post/Media Line (own Oct 24 piece) = 3 declared families. Restoration fact is the Ukrainian government's own primary claim, carried by the wire.
sections.what_disputed: Neither Musk nor the US government acknowledged ordering the restriction; Trump said Musk 'put it back' on Oct 22, a claim Ukrainian officials disputed at the time; the ministry did not say service was fully restored, only speeds; the cause of the restriction and of its removal remain undisclosed.
sections.why_matters: One company switched Ukraine's drone shield back on — and nobody will say who switched it off. 160 kph to 400+ overnight.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (in-window, Reuters Sat Oct 24) -- Ukraine says Starlink/Starshield fully restored after 10+ days of throttling; speeds back above 400 kph

totw_analysis: Our read: One company switched Ukraine's drone shield back on — and nobody will say who switched it off. 160 kph to 400+ overnight. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Who should control an army's internet — a private billionaire, or the state paying for the war? Social debate is dominated by distrust of Trump/Musk statements ('lying, again') and calls to replace Starlink.
